title: Abaqus Explicit deformable-body to rigid-surface finite sliding
purpose: Turn the first bounded AgentFEM explicit rigid-contact route into an externally anchored verification obligation without introducing a forming-specific solver or claiming that a different finite-element discretization reproduces Abaqus pointwise output.
physics: two-stage explicit normal contact followed by penalty Coulomb sliding against a rigid surface

source.title: Finite-sliding contact between a deformable body and a rigid surface

stages: establish frictionless contact under the normal load

execution.structural_api: Surface and RigidBody -> RigidContactPair -> contact Operator -> explicit Procedure -> accepted State -> Result/Verification
execution.evidence: The fixed public protocol, parameter identity, force/friction assessor, fail-closed cases, finite sliding across triangle facets, accepted friction State, restart, and two-rank component consistency are automated; the complete deformable finite-element external comparison remains pending.
execution.current_evidence: The fixed public protocol, parameter identity, force/friction assessor, fail-closed cases, finite sliding across triangle facets, accepted friction State, restart, and two-rank component consistency are automated.
execution.missing_evidence: A complete deformable finite-element time history using the fixed protocol has not yet produced a SimulationResult with mesh/time convergence and serial/MPI endpoint comparison.

observables: normal contact resultant versus applied normal load
tangential contact resultant versus the Coulomb cap
active, sliding, and invalid contact-point counts
facet crossings under finite sliding over a tessellated rigid surface
recoverable contact energy and irreversible frictional dissipation
acceptance: The model uses the fixed public material, load, friction, and sliding parameters or declares a separate derived benchmark identity.
Normal contact force balances the applied normal load within the declared tolerance.
Sliding tangential force lies on the Coulomb cap within the declared tolerance.
Contact action and reaction close within the declared tolerance.
At least one point is active and sliding; no projection is invalid.
A tessellated-tool variant crosses at least one rigid facet without changing slave-point identity.
Frictional dissipation is nonnegative and remains distinct from recoverable penalty energy.
The complete finite-element result passes time-step refinement and serial/two-rank comparison before promotion.
limitations: The current automated assessor and component tests define the gate but do not yet satisfy the complete finite-element external benchmark.
The Abaqus Explicit reference uses B31 beam contact; AgentFEM must not present a tetrahedral solid trace as a pointwise beam-output reproduction.
This benchmark does not verify deformable-to-deformable contact, curved-normal geometric stiffness, implicit friction linearization, self-contact, shells, or plastic forming.
